implement: legion-worker: PR body template, E2E proof lines, red-then-green proof at the head, pushing, and the production check after the close (references/pr-body.md, merge-gate.md).
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass pr-body.md requires over the settled 38-place migration before the implementer's proof.
dispatch: posting the production-check output on INFRA-440 with dispatch message.
test: legion-worker: the tester drives the browser suite and the pages on the INFRA-42/INFRA-43 pod harness, tries to break the component, and reads CI for static checks (references/pr-body.md).
review: legion-worker: review submission, threads and the merge gate (references/review-threads.md, merge-gate.md).
ce-simplify-code: judging whether the migration left duplicate wrappers or dead code (LiveDot, FreshnessDot, per-site live links, refs/actor.ts re-exports).

summary: One module features/refs/AgentName.tsx (link, control and static variants; running / not-running / unknown from the registry; one shell-level poller) replaces the per-place agent markup in 38 inventoried places; a Biome noRestrictedImports guard plus an rg audit and the inventory prove no place draws its own; packages/dispatch/e2e/agent-name.e2e.ts is the red-then-green acceptance in chromium and iphone.
decisions: D1 one polling owner in the app shell instead of per-hook intervals.
D2 the Agents page FreshnessDot and its 2-10 minute amber tier are dropped; age moves to the state mark's title.
D3 Claimed by keeps its visible 'not running' words (claim is free to take) beside the component's state.
D4 subscribers' running state comes from the registry, not Subscriber.live.
D5 the @-mention picker shows the component without a link (role=option inside a listbox).

findings.finding: The universal outcome reaches additional Delivery displays, not just the session-groups editor. The survey identifies omitted displays that the proposed migration does not name. Some have session IDs available; others are title-based aggregates for which a unique live-conversation destination is not established.
findings.answer: Plan inventory row 38 migrates DrillDown's raw session ids (L per id); the Parent agent facet, lanes, PR list and drill-down Parent agent(s) are named exclusions: their value is a title, group or placeholder, never a session id (parentAgent.ts:12, dispatch-api.ts:2774-2782).

findings.finding: The control variant does not yet account for two substantial link ancestors: ReplyQuote and BroadcastsPage rows. Simply replacing their author text with a default AgentName creates nested anchors; putting the separate link beside the name but inside the existing ancestor still violates 'never inside another control.'
findings.answer: Rows 7 and 32: ReplyQuote renders the author with AgentName outside the quote link (the excerpt keeps the parent-turn link; ReplyTarget carries the Actor for the composer); BroadcastsPage renders the sender outside the row link, which keeps its broadcast destination.

findings.finding: The proposed static variant is not one uniform exception. A noninteractive tooltip and the live page's self-heading have existing reasons not to navigate; a mention option performs a distinct selection action and falls under the spec's adjacent-link rule unless deliberately excluded. Role mention options also display the holder's agent title in their detail text, not just session-option titles.
findings.answer: Static variant split into three named exclusions with separate reasons: E1 tooltip (AGENTS.md:276 never interactive), E2 mention picker (role=option inside role=listbox; a link inside or beside an option breaks listbox semantics; every option is a listed agent; role-option holder detail drawn the same way), E3 the live page's own header (self).

findings.finding: A string hook is suitable for attributes and authored text, but not a substitute for the component in visible sentences. Several consumers erase identity into strings before rendering; migrating them also reaches quote previews, artifact-name linking, assistant-ui metadata readers, and frozen reply targets. These downstream contracts need to be named, not just the string producers.
findings.answer: Section 'Strings that become structured' names each producer/consumer pair: activity parts with LinkedName on text parts, event-description parts, describeAskResolution as a component, askTurnLabel returning the actor, ReplyQuote/ReplyTarget carrying the Actor, dispatch-marks author metadata encoder and decoder changed together; mentionDisplay text and its offsets unchanged; useAgentText only for attributes, document title, dialogs, textarea text, clipboard, empty state.

findings.finding: Recipient identity must remain distinct from a mutable role target. The proposed sentence refactor must not resolve every historical role reference to its current holder, nor turn a role with no resolved session into a fabricated agent link.
findings.answer: Delivery lines render AgentName for the recorded recipient session id; role addresses stay role text; retry resolution through the current stored target unchanged; an earlier attempt keeps linking the session it reached; route `role:` stays text.

findings.finding: 'Running now' needs a precise observational meaning. The approved source is registry membership, but neither a 15-second poll nor Subscriber.live is a process-level probe. Subscriber.live is another snapshot of the same listener session list, so mixing it with the component's separately refreshed registry can produce contradictory dots. Existing freshness and stream-connection indicators describe different facts.
findings.answer: Running defined as listed in the latest successful registry read, not a process probe; subscribers use the registry (D4) and keep the endpoint for membership, last_seen, removable, stored title; live page stream dot kept and labelled as the connection; FreshnessDot removal and the lost amber tier recorded as D2, age kept in the state mark's title.

findings.finding: The pending/error behavior is under-specified, especially after a previously successful registry read. 'Nothing while registry pending/error' avoids a false Not running signal, but gives no indication that running state is unknown and leaves unanswered whether cached titles or prior presence remain usable. Credentials currently have an explicit unknown contract.
findings.answer: Three states specified: unknown while pending or when the latest read failed (also after an earlier success), never shown as not running, dashed neutral ring 'Running state unknown'; cached titles still name the agent; credentials and ClaimChip use the same state; unit tests cover pending, error-before-success, error-after-success.

findings.finding: 'One shared ["agents"] query' does not establish the promised polling cost by itself. Calling useAgents(true, true) in every name and every string hook also enables reads for non-session actors and constructs a complete titles Map per hook instance. The endpoint is not a lightweight membership read: it also runs two database aggregates.
findings.answer: D1: one polling owner (AgentRegistryPoller in app.tsx) driven by a mount counter; useAgents loses its per-observer interval; module hook reads ['agents'] without an interval, enabled only for session subjects, one derived lookup per response; fake-timer unit test bounds the cadence with staggered mounts; e2e asserts one registry fetch on load, no per-session request, and a rename/stop seen without reload.

findings.finding: The proposed dot is accessible text for a screen reader, but remains a color-only distinction for a sighted reader who cannot distinguish its colors. Removing ClaimChip's visible 'not running' text makes that regression concrete. A role=img label does not make a color-only difference visible on a phone.
findings.answer: Non-colour distinction: running filled dot, not running hollow ring, unknown dashed ring, each role=img with an accessible label; ClaimChip keeps its visible 'not running' words (D3); component tests assert labels and shapes; phone run checks the stopped state.

findings.finding: Phone acceptance needs to choose between ordinary controls and inline sentence links. An ordinary anchor acquires a 44×44 minimum and inline-flex layout below 1280px; an inline link follows a deliberately different hit-box convention. Applying either indiscriminately can break byline alignment, truncation, or adjacent kept actions.
findings.answer: Inline names use .dispatch-inline-link (styles.css:105); standalone and control-variant live links keep the 44 px floor below md; hosts keep their own truncation/wrapping; e2e at 390 checks no page widening, claim shrink, non-overlapping ask-card button and live link, and Agents names whole via existing agents.e2e.ts.

findings.finding: Adding agent links introduces a keyboard-navigation invariant that the four primary acceptance surfaces do not cover. List and Board open commands click the first anchor in the row/card. Their current title-first DOM order makes the proposed later ClaimChip link safe, but that ordering must remain intentional.
findings.answer: IssueList.tsx:127 and IssueBoard.tsx:589,599 switch from querySelector('a') to an explicit data-issue-link selector; e2e adds claimed List row and Board card: o/Enter open the issue, the agent link opens the live page, an iphone tap on the Board card's agent link navigates without a drag.

findings.finding: The browser acceptance asks for 'the current title' on both running and stopped agents, whereas the outcome promises a current title only while running and today's fallback otherwise. A stopped session has no current registry title to read. The criterion also does not state how to demonstrate live-title precedence rather than accidentally accepting identical stamped/live titles.
findings.answer: Fixture matrix: running session with different live and stamped titles (expects live), stopped session (expects stamped), untitled stopped (expects short id), an owner write (suffix), user actors unchanged by unit tests; ids differ in their first 8 characters; rename and stop while the page is open, seen within 30 s without reload.

findings.finding: The proposed import restriction is narrower than the architecture guarantee. It can reject direct imports and direct re-exports from @legion/contracts, but it does not prove that a relative barrel, external wrapper, or hand-built agent label is absent. The actual SPA imports predominantly use ../refs/actor, including ./actor at another depth. Test files and a pure canonical-reference formatter also need an explicit migration policy.
findings.answer: Lint: noRestrictedImports on @legion/contracts naming functions for packages/dispatch/web/src/** at error, exempting only AgentName.tsx and routes.ts (reference short form); refs/actor.ts re-exports removed so no relative barrel remains; test files not exempt; naming tests move to packages/contracts/src/actor-label.test.ts; negative proof for named, aliased, namespace and re-export forms from root and package lint, any uncaught form recorded.

findings.finding: 'No place ... draws an agent with its own markup' has no decisive machine oracle as written. Absence of four helper imports is not equivalent to component adoption: raw .title, .session_id, locally named formatters, and existing flattened strings all bypass that check. A one-off rg command also has no stated expected result or CI owner.
findings.answer: The check is stated honestly as three parts: the lint guard (imports/re-exports confined), an rg audit with its expected hits listed, and the inventory table with call sites in the PR for the reviewer; AGENT_LIVE_PATH restriction added if Biome patterns catch relative specifiers, else audited.

findings.finding: The required red run is feasible without a second workspace, but the proposed 'red commit first then green' does not yet identify the product build under test or protect the baseline bundle. The normal e2e command rebuilds the current SPA; the local server rereads web/dist. A later run against the same directory can therefore silently test head instead of baseline.
findings.answer: Red/green without a second workspace: commit the spec alone on the base, build the base SPA, keep a copy in $TMPDIR/infra440/dist-base, run chromium and iphone, require a behaviour-assertion failure, record product and test SHAs; any later spec change re-runs red against the kept base build; green at head, then the full suite; harness per INFRA-42/INFRA-43/LEGION-695 docs.

findings.finding: Production acceptance names neither the changed page nor its backing routes, and merge does not itself deploy Dispatch. A health/version check alone would not identify which reader-facing path was checked. The supplied deployment rule provides the command, but its arguments and the manual deployment handoff still need a concrete answer.
findings.answer: Production check: --page /issues/INFRA-440 --route /api/v1/agents --route /api/v1/issues/INFRA-440 with the merged SHA; output on the PR and the issue; no automatic Dispatch deploy (INFRA-64), so an undeployed build is recorded as such and reported pending until the deploy wake. No production click-through: the deployment rules say the check never claims a person looked and the browser test proves the behaviour.

findings.finding: The cutover must update documentation that currently directs future code back to refs/actor.ts and describes behavior the planner intends to remove. Updating only implementation/tests would leave a competing convention in the repository's own agent instructions.
findings.answer: Order step 6 updates packages/dispatch/AGENTS.md: a 'How an agent is shown' paragraph plus the follower/subscriber LiveDot paragraph (:274), the refs/actor.ts naming boundary (:389-390), credential lines (:436-439) and the Agents row Open link/freshness dot; copy handles, tooltip noninteractivity, reference short form and host wrapping rules stay; contracts CHANGELOG only if contracts' exports change.
